claims.text: The untreated material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with an FCC/B2 dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
Warm or cold rolling introduces a high dislocation density in the FCC lamellae.
Rolling followed by annealing can selectively recrystallize FCC regions while leaving much of the B2 phase unrecrystallized.
A rolling reduction of 30–50% is suitable for the proposed treatment.
Annealing for approximately 5–15 minutes at approximately 800 °C will produce the targeted selective recrystallization.
The treatment maintains coherent interfaces in the B2 phase.
Partial recrystallization produces ultrafine or refined FCC grains while preserving portions of the lamellar B2 framework.
Partial FCC recrystallization reduces dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
Locally softened and refined FCC lamellae accommodate plastic flow more effectively.
Improved plastic accommodation in the FCC lamellae impedes crack initiation at boundaries.
Retained hard B2 lamellae maintain or increase the alloy's strength after treatment.
The treated alloy will retain a tensile strength of at least 1.5–1.8 GPa.
The treated alloy will achieve more than 20% elongation to failure at room temperature.
Cryo-deformation and annealing have previously increased both strength and ductility relative to as-cast material in this eutectic alloy system.
The untreated as-cast alloy typically has approximately 1.5 GPa tensile strength and approximately 10% tensile elongation.
The proposed performance applies to ambient-temperature, quasi-static tensile loading.
Excessive annealing time or temperature will coarsen both phases and reduce strengthening.
High-temperature service can cause boundary coarsening that diminishes the enhanced ductility.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires elongation above 20%, but the falsification rule only rejects elongation below 15%; results from 15% through 20% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
